text:
cheng: quick heads-up — noticed a p95 spike for /chat/compose (prod, us-east) after kernel-selector v2 rollout (~03:12). p95 jumped from ~92ms -> 210ms for small-context requests.

maria: can you paste the perf profile?

cheng: pasted snippet from perf tools: 
```
# top 5 flame functions
kernel_selector::choose_kernel_for_batch +45%
batcher::form_microbatch (avg size 2.1 tokens) +28%
kv_cache::evict_hot_prefixes +12%
runtime::serialize_request +8%
```

alex: that smells like the selector prefers a kernel that has worse cold-start for very short sequences — causes more frequent prefetch / kv churn. did the selector change kernel affinity heuristics?

cheng: yep — the new cost model trades off throughput at longer seq for slightly lower cost. it ends up preferring the fused attention kernel that has a heavier setup path for short sequences. also saw KV hitrate drop ~7% (more evictions).

sam: did we also change batch formation? if batches are smaller it's worse for the heavier kernel.

cheng: we did a tweak to the microbatch split thresholds last week to reduce tail latency at 95th for large seq, but it seems to interact poorly w/ this kernel. batcher metrics show an uptick in 1-2 request microbatches.

kevin: proposal: introduce a route-tier driven token budget cap that biases the scheduler to pick a lighter kernel for routes with median seq < 64. fallback path if p95 goes over target: temporarily bump token budget for that route to favor larger microbatching and prefer the throughput kernel. example config snippet: 
```
routes:
  /chat/compose:
    tier: standard
    token_budget: 48  # default
    kernel_policy:
      prefer_light_for_median_lt: 64
      fallback_token_boost: 96
      fallback_window_s: 120
```

maria: +1. we should also gate this behind a canary on a subset of pods. don't want a global flip.

alex: for the canary, we can set route-tier hash modulo 100 < 5 to get ~5% traffic. we should collect p95, batch_size_dist, kv_hitrate.

cheng: I sketched an experiment plan: rollout canary -> monitor 15m p95 & kv hits -> if p95 improves and kv hitrate stable -> scale canary -> full rollout. if p95 degrades, auto-fallback.

sam: one more safety: add a kernel-affinity override table as emergency kill-switch so we can pin kernels per machine class. e.g. prefer_kernel: fast-path-quant on gpuv2 nodes.

kevin: agreed. here's the quick emergency knob (hot patch): 
```
/ops/kernel_affinity_overrides
  gpuv2:
    prefer_kernel: fast-path-quant
    enforced: true
```
deploy-bot: deploy started: kernel-affinity-rollback-config -> canary pods (tag: canary-kpolicy-2026-03-18)

maria: monitoring dashboards created -> p95, batch_size, kv_hitrate, kernel_choice_ratio. alert if p95 > 140ms for 5m or kv_hitrate drops > 10%.

alex: next actions: 1) run canary (cheng) 2) collect 30m of metrics (maria) 3) if stable, bump token_budget and kernel policy gradually (kevin). I'll own the rollforward decision.

cheng: starting canary now. will post logs and a quick csv of batch sizes after 10m.

sam: thanks all. @kevin @alex if it looks hot we can flip the affinity override and rollback the selector change as last resort. :thumbsup:
